clue.text: After merger of firms, have a drink

indicators.note: a merger joins two firms into one, so the word for a firm is written twice side by side

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Once the companies have merged, the staff celebrate with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merger of' doubles CO, the abbreviation for a firm; 'have' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate beverage made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: Whipped, sing badly

parts.note: to chant is to sing
illy is an old adverb meaning badly

explanation.surface: Someone who was beaten sings poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whipped' looks like punishment; it describes cream, as in the French dessert topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Chantilly cream is sweetened beaten cream, so the name serves as an adjective for whisked.

clue.text: Supply queen, perhaps, and king

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, an example signalled by perhaps
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: Provisions for a queen, maybe, and a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' suggests ER, but here it is a female cat, and ER is the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide food and drink for guests, a verb synonym.

clue.text: For sustenance, worker eats fruit

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so the fruit goes into the worker

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: An employee snacks on fruit to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment or food, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Quick to pass the amendment

indicators.note: an amendment alters a text, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to pass a parliamentary amendment without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amendment' rearranges TOPASSTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Done with the greatest possible speed, an adverb meaning very fast.

clue.text: In French city, a down-and-out

parts.note: Pau is a city in south-west France
a in the sense of each, as in five pounds a head, means per

explanation.surface: A tramp living in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link word; 'a' is PER, as in 'ten pounds a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A destitute person, a noun synonym for vagrant.

clue.text: Fantastic mincepies — I removed a sample

indicators.note: fantastic means wild or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged
removed says the letter named is taken away from the fodder

explanation.surface: Wonderful seasonal pastries, one of which I took as a taster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I removed' takes one I from MINCEPIES; 'Fantastic' rearranges the remaining MNCEPIES.
explanation.definitionFit: An example taken for testing, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Where to .find water monster supported by conservationists

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by puts one piece below the other

parts.note: the Hydra was the many-headed monster of Greek myth
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A water monster backed by environmental campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray dot before 'find' is a printing mark. NT is the National Trust, which looks after historic British buildings and land.
explanation.definitionFit: A street fire plug from which firefighters draw their supply.

clue.text: Serial featuring a poet carried by rail

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the poet goes within the bird

parts.note: the sora is a small North American rail, a marsh bird
Alexander Pope was an English poet

explanation.surface: A serial story about a poet travelling by train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' looks like the railway; it is the bird family, of which the sora is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running broadcast drama in episodes.

clue.text: Spot on demand

definitions.meaning: to demand is to insist on and obtain, as in requiring payment

explanation.definitionFit: Both precise (adjective) and to extract or require (verb).

clue.text: Volunteers rejected praise — that's characteristic

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters for the volunteers are read backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
a tribute is an expression of praise

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers turning down a compliment is said to be typical of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns TA (the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve) into AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality or feature typical of someone; noun sense.

clue.text: A short first play

indicators.note: first says the drink comes before the letter A

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a dram

explanation.surface: A brief opening performance in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' is a noun here, a nip of spirits, not an adjective shortening something; 'first' puts DRAM before A.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage piece for actors is a theatrical work.

clue.text: Harris and Co. met in a bar, the one that's been done up

indicators.note: something done up is renovated, so the letters of the preceding words are reworked

parts.words: met in a bar, the one

explanation.surface: Harris and friends meet in a pub that has been renovated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's been done up' rearranges METINABARTHEONE. Harris is one of the three title characters of Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel of a Thames boating trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Harris is one of the trio in Jerome K. Jerome's novel, so he and his companions are its titular figures.

clue.text: See about the empty place

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
CA stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its first and last letters, its middle removed

explanation.surface: Look around the vacant spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves TE from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something is to find its position, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Drink taken after drug engenders severe measures

indicators.note: taken after places the drink behind the drug

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: Drinking after taking drugs brings stern consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engenders' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden tough official campaign of suppression.

clue.text: Set table in a fashion, showing restraint

indicators.note: in a fashion means arranged in some way, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Laying a dinner table stylishly while showing some self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a fashion' rearranges SETTABLE; 'showing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A car safety strap holds the passenger back in a crash, a physical restraint.

clue.text: Political leader, a head following Eastern philosophy mostly

indicators.note: following places the second piece behind the first
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Taoism is the Chinese philosophy of the Way
a head, as in a pound a head, means each

explanation.surface: A leader who follows Eastern teachings for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the M of TAOISM. The answer is the title of the Irish prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish prime minister's official title.

clue.text: Pass along one road as a settler

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
on can mean along, as in getting on
I is the Roman numeral one
ST is street, a road

explanation.surface: Traveller passing along a road to start a new life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who settles in a new territory.

clue.text: Time to reserve an updated publication

parts.note: a year is a period of time
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: It is time to put a hold on the latest edition of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual volume, reissued every twelve months with fresh information.

clue.text: Cloth needs tack to hold it up

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the reversed word goes inside

parts.note: to baste is to tack, sew with long loose stitches

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Fabric must be tacked to keep it in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses IT to TI; 'needs' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine light linen or cotton fabric.

clue.text: Book reveals after a month eggs have turned

indicators.note: after places the eggs behind the month

parts.note: OCT is the abbreviation for October

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the word for eggs is read backwards

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: A book reveals that a month later the eggs had gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have turned' reverses OVA to give AVO; 'reveals' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A book size in which each printed sheet is folded into eight leaves.

clue.text: Partnership's accountant laughs loudly

definitions.note: the apostrophe s stands for is, so the partnership is what the wordplay makes

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
to hoot is to laugh loudly

explanation.surface: The firm's accountant bursts out laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partnership's' reads as a possessive, but it means 'Partnership is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In cahoots means in secret league, so the word denotes a collusive alliance.

clue.text: Artist put up for a prize

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: a drawer is someone who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist is nominated for an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given in recognition, a synonym for prize as a noun.

clue.text: Become fond of somebody — female with railways to run

parts.note: to take to someone is to grow fond of them
she is the female pronoun
ELS are elevated railways, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: Someone falls for a woman who loves trains and then flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for fleeing, running away quickly.

clue.text: Issue with protective headgear and cape

parts.note: a topi is a sun helmet worn in hot countries
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: A problem involving a helmet and a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a garment; it is the map abbreviation C.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject of discussion, a matter or theme.

clue.text: Inspiration for songs of love, and some of anger — a toreador

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A muse inspires love songs, and a bullfighter's anger too.
explanation.walkthrough: Erato is the Greek muse of lyric and love poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek Muse of lyric and erotic poetry.

clue.text: Devout pope, filled with love

indicators.note: filled with says the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: Pius is the name taken by several popes
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A pope who is full of love is devout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is O, the zero score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Religiously devoted, a direct adjective synonym.

clue.text: An aroma — it can make a woman loved

indicators.note: can make says the letters before may be formed into a new word

explanation.surface: A scent can win a woman's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' rearranges ANAROMAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A female lover or sweetheart, from the Italian for beloved.

clue.text: Happy with what lies inside England's borders

parts.note: the content of something is what it holds

indicators.note: borders are the edges of a word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Feeling satisfied with life in the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' takes ED from 'England's'; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfied, at ease, synonym for glad.

clue.text: Either part of Sinai?

parts.note: split the mountain's name into its two pieces: the first is a wrongdoing that idleness is counted among, the second is a three-toed tree mammal of that name

explanation.surface: A question about splitting a mountain in two.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN + AI: idleness is one of the seven deadly sins, and the ai is a three-toed animal of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a deadly sin (laziness) and a slow tree-dwelling mammal, matching each half.
